title: Reusable infrastructure for potential automorphy over CM fields, Part II: Dwork switching motives
summary: Target-level plan of the Dwork pencil and general exponent data, specialized monodromy, determinants, local Hodge theory and switching for the selected zero-shaped asymmetric and self-dual systems. General-character ordinarity remains conditional on maximal nilpotence and consecutive labelled weights. All 81 targets are specified; ten explicit proof/supplier gaps and pending upstream imports remain. This is a reviewed mathematical plan, not a claim of formalization or of completed proofs.
readme: The definitive reader is research/blueprint/readmes/PotentialAutomorphyDworkMotivesPartII.md. DM.0–DM.1 give the finite algebra and Dwork data; DM.2–DM.3 construct the eigensheaves and hypergeometric comparison; DM.4–DM.5 treat complex/residual monodromy and finite étale level torsors; DM.6–DM.7 treat determinants, compatible Frobenius polynomials and local Hodge theory; DM.8 gives potential semistable models and conditional ordinarity; DM.9 specifies the three switching constructions. Strong monodromy and consecutive-weight conclusions concern the selected zero-shaped data, with a separate self-dual rank-two construction. The recorded proof gaps remain requirements. Automorphy lifting is consumed from its existing owners.

stages.title: Linear algebra and finite linear groups
stages.description: Targets: Pseudo-reflections and transvections (DM.0/pseudo-reflection); Rank-one difference of companion matrices (DM.0/companion-normal-form); Levelt's rigidity theorem for hypergeometric triples (DM.0/levelt-rigidity); Irreducibility of hypergeometric groups (DM.0/hypergeometric-group-irreducible); Finite unitary groups (DM.0/finite-unitary-group); Hermitian and skew-Hermitian forms over a quadratic extension (DM.0/hermitian-form); Uniqueness of nondegenerate Hermitian forms over finite fields (DM.0/hermitian-forms-unique); Conjugate self-dual absolutely irreducible representations are unitary (DM.0/conjugate-self-dual-is-unitary); Normal subgroups of SL_n and SU_n over finite fields (DM.0/special-linear-unitary-simple); Simple linear groups in different characteristics are not isomorphic (DM.0/artin-non-isomorphism); Irreducible groups generated by transvections (Zalesskii–Serezhkin), in the form used (DM.0/zalesskii-serezhkin-classification); Surjectivity onto a product of two groups with distinct simple quotients (DM.0/product-of-simple-images). Remaining proof inputs: Finite classical-group classification, unitary generation and cross-characteristic orders.

stages.title: The Dwork pencil and its exponent data
stages.description: Targets: Auxiliary moduli with prescribed order of l (DM.1/auxiliary-modulus); The Dwork pencil of hypersurfaces (DM.1/dwork-pencil); Symmetry groups of the Dwork pencil and their characters (DM.1/dwork-symmetry-groups); Exponent data and the complementary index set (DM.1/dwork-exponent-datum); Trivial multiplicative stabiliser of Qian's index set (DM.1/asymmetric-stabiliser-trivial); The quotient family over the thrice-punctured line (DM.1/three-punctured-cover). The target-level statements and direct supplier interfaces are specified in the reader.

stages.title: Eigen-local-systems of the Dwork pencil
stages.description: Targets: Cohomology of the Fermat hypersurface (DM.2/fermat-hypersurface-cohomology); Integral cohomology of smooth hypersurfaces is torsion-free (DM.2/integral-cohomology-torsion-free); The Dwork eigen-local-systems V_λ, V[𝔫] and V_B (DM.2/dwork-eigensheaves); Poincaré duality between conjugate eigensheaves (DM.2/eigensheaf-duality); Real forms of the self-dual Dwork eigensheaves (DM.2/self-dual-real-forms); Splitting of the Fermat fibre into eigenlines (DM.2/fermat-fibre-splitting); The Dwork eigensheaves are locally free of rank n (DM.2/eigensheaf-rank). The target-level statements and direct supplier interfaces are specified in the reader.

stages.title: Katz's hypergeometric description
stages.description: Targets: Katz's hypergeometric sheaf attached to a Dwork exponent datum (DM.3/katz-hypergeometric-sheaf); Basic properties of the hypergeometric sheaf (DM.3/hypergeometric-sheaf-properties); Local monodromy of the hypergeometric sheaf (DM.3/hypergeometric-local-monodromy); Katz's comparison of Dwork eigensheaves with hypergeometric sheaves (DM.3/katz-dwork-comparison); The twisting character comes from an algebraic Hecke character (DM.3/twisting-hecke-character); The twisted Dwork local systems W_λ (DM.3/twisted-dwork-local-system). Remaining proof inputs: Hypergeometric convolution rank, local monodromy and determinant; Recognition and coefficient control of the comparison character.

stages.title: Complex monodromy
stages.description: Targets: The Dwork monodromy representations and peripheral loops (DM.4/dwork-monodromy-representations); Monodromy at zero: eigenvalues ζ_N^b, b ∈ B (DM.4/monodromy-at-zero); Monodromy at one: Picard–Lefschetz (DM.4/picard-lefschetz-at-one); Monodromy at infinity is unipotent (DM.4/unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity); Companion-matrix model of the Dwork monodromy (DM.4/companion-model-of-monodromy); Maximally unipotent monodromy at infinity (DM.4/maximal-unipotent-monodromy-at-infinity); Absolute irreducibility of the residual monodromy (DM.4/residual-monodromy-absolutely-irreducible). Remaining proof inputs: Hypergeometric convolution rank, local monodromy and determinant.

stages.title: Residual monodromy and level-structure torsors
stages.description: Targets: Full special linear residual monodromy (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sl); Full symplectic residual monodromy of the self-dual family (DM.5/residual-monodromy-sp); The skew-Hermitian Poincaré pairing on the residual Dwork local system (DM.5/hermitian-poincare-pairing); Full special unitary residual monodromy in the unitary case (DM.5/residual-monodromy-su); The determinant of the Dwork local systems is geometrically constant (DM.5/determinant-descends); Moduli of level structures on Dwork local systems (DM.5/level-structure-torsor); Residual monodromy at two primes is the full product (DM.5/two-prime-product-monodromy); The level-structure torsors are geometrically irreducible (DM.5/level-structure-torsor-irreducible). Remaining proof inputs: Finite classical-group classification, unitary generation and cross-characteristic orders.

stages.title: Frobenius, Gauss sums and determinants
stages.description: Targets: Frobenius on the Fermat eigenlines is a product of Gauss sums (DM.6/fermat-frobenius-gauss-sums); Gauss-sum formula for the determinant of the Dwork motive (DM.6/dwork-determinant-gauss-formula); The Gauss-sum product descends to the cyclotomic coefficients (DM.6/gauss-product-descent); The determinant of the residual Dwork motive is an n-th power up to 𝔽_{l²} (DM.6/determinant-nth-power); Matching determinants at the coefficient prime l (DM.6/determinant-matching-at-l); Matching determinants at the auxiliary prime l′ ≡ 1 mod N (DM.6/determinant-matching-at-auxiliary-prime); Frobenius polynomials of Dwork fibres are integral and independent of λ (DM.6/frobenius-polynomials-independent). Remaining proof inputs: Equivariant correspondence comparison.

stages.title: p-adic Hodge theory and local monodromy of the fibres
stages.description: Targets: Twisted de Rham eigenspaces of the Dwork family (DM.7/twisted-de-rham-eigenspaces); Hodge grades of the Fermat eigenlines (DM.7/hodge-grades-of-fermat-eigenlines); Consecutive Hodge numbers of the Dwork motives (DM.7/consecutive-hodge-numbers); Dwork fibres are de Rham with consecutive labelled Hodge–Tate weights (DM.7/dwork-hodge-tate-weights); Crystallinity and Frobenius at good-reduction fibres (DM.7/crystalline-at-good-reduction); Ordinarity of fibres near the Fermat point when l ≡ 1 mod N (DM.7/ordinary-near-fermat-point); Inertia on the Fermat fibre when l ≡ −1 mod N (DM.7/fermat-fibre-inertia-at-minus-one); Maximal unipotent local monodromy at places with v(t) < 0 (DM.7/steinberg-monodromy-away-from-coefficient-prime); The Dwork fibres form weakly compatible systems (DM.7/dwork-compatible-system); Generic slopes of indecomposable lisse sheaves (Drinfeld–Kedlaya) (DM.7/drinfeld-kedlaya-slope-bound); Generic crystalline ordinarity of the Dwork family (DM.7/generic-crystalline-ordinarity). Remaining proof inputs: Tame specialization and curvewise crystalline companions.

stages.title: Semistable models and ordinarity near infinity
stages.description: Targets: The equivariant semistable blowup of the reciprocal Dwork family (DM.8/dwork-semistable-blowup); Equivariant semistable models of Dwork fibres near infinity (DM.8/equivariant-semistable-model); The log special fibre of the semistable model lifts over W[T] (DM.8/log-special-fibre-witt-lift); Hyodo–Kato description of D_st of Dwork fibres near infinity (DM.8/hyodo-kato-description-near-infinity); Regular ordinarity of Dwork fibres near infinity (DM.8/ordinary-near-infinity); Regular ordinarity of Dwork motives near infinity for a general character (DM.8/conditional-regular-ordinarity). Remaining proof inputs: General-character ordinarity remains conditional; Equivariant toroidal subdivision.

stages.title: Switching theorems
stages.description: Targets: Determinant twists, the module W and the torsor T_W for Qian's switch (DM.9/switching-determinant-data); Weil restriction of the torsor and the local valuation conditions (DM.9/weil-restricted-local-conditions); Qian's switching theorem for non-self-dual Dwork motives (DM.9/qian-switching-theorem); Switching in the self-dual Dwork family (DM.9/self-dual-switching); Local constancy of Galois representations in the Dwork family (Kisin) (DM.9/kisin-local-constancy); Reductions of two-dimensional crystalline representations of small weight (Berger) (DM.9/berger-reduction-small-weight); Local Dwork points with prescribed reductions (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne) (DM.9/bcgnt-local-dwork-points); The CM-induced auxiliary system R_CM (DM.9/cm-induced-seed); Choice of primes and fields for the p–r switch (DM.9/bcgnt-switching-primes); The auxiliary Dwork systems R_aux and S_UA (Boxer–Calegari–Gee–Newton–Thorne) (DM.9/bcgnt-auxiliary-dwork-systems); The auxiliary system R_aux in rank two via twisted modular curves (DM.9/rank-two-auxiliary-system). Remaining proof inputs: Twisted modular-curve rank-two construction; Fixed finite coefficient field in root extraction; Nonarchimedean local inverse for a finite étale cover.

upstreamImports.contract: Finite étale covers of a connected scheme correspond to finite continuous π₁-sets; finite lisse coefficient modules give continuous representations, and connected covers correspond to transitive actions. ECF §F.0.2.
For geometrically connected qc X/k, 1→π₁(X_kbar)→π₁(X)→G_k→1 is exact, with rational-point sections up to geometric conjugation. ECF §F.0.A2.
Proper base change for arbitrary torsion coefficients, compatible with coefficient maps, cup products and finite group actions. ECF §F.2.1.
Finite constructible cohomology for the stated finite-type/invertible coefficient regime; smooth proper lissity and fibre transport. ECF §F.3. This does not itself prove integral torsion-freeness.

Normalized integral adic realization and finite-E rational realization, with stable lattices, derived inverse-limit control and finite-dimensional proper cohomology; compatibility with base change, cup products and group actions. ECF §§F.4.1–F.4.6.

Smooth purity, trace and Poincaré pairings in the stated smooth proper invertible-coefficient domain. Integral perfectness here also uses the hypersurface torsion-free argument; EDC.2 explicitly retains the general Ext correction. ECF §F.6.
External tensor products, compact-support projection and Künneth, with the boundedness, finite-Tor and coefficient hypotheses used for the convolution. ECF §F.2.7.
Separated finite-type constructible lower shriek, base change, composition and compactification independence at finite levels, then normalized adic realization. ECF §§F.2.4–F.2.6 and F.4.

Finite ordinary and compact Artin comparison for complex algebraic schemes, plus proper relative Rf* and separated Rf! exchange on ctf inputs, compatible with cup products, finite groups and monodromy. CPC ComplexComparison Layers10 and12.
Pass finite Artin comparison to integral adic and finite-E rational realizations; keep the stable-lattice essential-image condition. CPC EllAdicRealization Layer10.

Grothendieck–Lefschetz for separated finite-type finite-field schemes with invertible finite ctf coefficients, and the rational corollary through adic realization; compatible with twists and finite group actions. CPC TraceFormula Layer11.
